report.summary: The namespace is failing at the database credential layer. PostgreSQL (Deployment postgresql) is running, initialized at 15:54:55-15:54:59Z from /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql, and it rejects new connections for user "otelu" with repeated FATAL password authentication failures starting 2026-11-21T15:55:47.231Z. Both database-backed application services fail on their own spans: product-catalog ListProducts/GetProduct return gRPC 13/5 with 'failed to load products: failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"', and product-reviews get_product_reviews returns psycopg2.OperationalError 'connection to server at "postgresql" (10.96.69.15), port 5432 failed: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "otelu"'. Frontend (500 on product, checkout, product-reviews and recommendations routes), frontend-proxy (500), recommendation (ListProducts failures) and checkout (PlaceOrder 13 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product') are failing as callers, and frontend application logs carry the same PostgreSQL error text. The credential context changed in the same seconds: Deployment accounting, product-reviews and product-catalog were the only workloads rolled to new ReplicaSets (15:55:39-15:55:51Z), and the new pod templates carry a 14-character DB password (identical in length to the value now in ConfigMap postgresql-init, 'otelp_7k9m2q4x') where the earlier templates carried a 5-character one, while a product-reviews DB-backed request still succeeded at 15:55:44.94Z. ConfigMap postgresql-init, the only object that defines the otelu password, was written again between 15:55:42Z and 15:55:47Z, after PostgreSQL had already initialized the role from its earlier content. The exact credential values in the Secret and in the container env are redacted, so which side holds the stale password cannot be read; the ConfigMap is named as the root-cause object and the mechanism is stated as a hypothesis.

claims.text: PostgreSQL logged repeated 'FATAL: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' entries, first at 2026-11-21T15:55:47.231Z and continuing through the end of the sampled window (last sampled 15:56:09.839Z), each with DETAIL 'Connection matched file "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_hba.conf" line 128: "host all all all scram-sha-256"'; 29 matching lines were returned for 15:55:47-15:56:09.

The postgresql pod's data directory was initialized at 15:54:55-15:54:59Z and the entrypoint logged 'running /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql', followed by CREATE ROLE, CREATE SCHEMA/TABLE, 'INSERT 0 50' (reviews) and 'INSERT 0 10' (catalog.products); the postgresql pod has existed since 15:54:52Z with 0 restarts, so the running otelu role was created by that init script.

product-reviews' own spans fail with psycopg2.OperationalError: span 'get_product_reviews' carries otel.status_description and exception.message 'connection to server at "postgresql" (10.96.69.15), port 5432 failed: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' (exception.type psycopg2.OperationalError, raised in /app/database.py fetch_product_reviews_from_db).

One product-reviews request (trace ad00729dca3db09bfaea6c9aef20c685) completed successfully at 15:55:44.94Z: oteldemo.ProductReviewService/GetProductReviews has rpc.grpc.status_code=0, its child get_product_reviews has no error detail and the frontend route returned http.status_code=200 - i.e. a database-backed review lookup succeeded about 2 seconds before the first FATAL entry.

frontend's own spans return HTTP 500 with otel.status_code=ERROR on GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/products/[productId]/index, POST /api/checkout, GET /api/product-reviews/[productId]/index and GET /api/recommendations, and frontend-proxy spans for the same requests record error=true http.status_code="500"; the frontend container log holds 50 matching error lines in 15:55:55-15:56:09Z including '5 NOT_FOUND: Product Not Found: L9ECAV7KIM' and 'failed to load products: failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"'.

checkout's own span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder fails with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and message 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"HQTGWGPNH4"', and its child client span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct returns rpc.grpc.status_code=5, i.e. checkout's failure is the product-catalog lookup failure.

recommendation's own spans fail: get_product_list raises grpc._channel._InactiveRpcError and its client span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts returns rpc.grpc.status_code=13 with details 'failed to load products: failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' (source line /app/recommendation_server.py:95 product_catalog_stub.ListProducts).

All 27 pods in astronomy-shop are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, including product-catalog-574776bb6-lnb6x, product-reviews-7cdd9d8df7-6g85v, postgresql-6bd9b846cb-4c94g and frontend-6859c775df-rkdzt, so pod readiness does not reflect the ongoing database authentication failures.

The cart path is not failing in the sampled traces: POST /api/cart returned http.status_code=200, oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and /GetCart returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and cart's valkey-cart:6379 spans carry no error, so cart and valkey-cart were checked and show no failure of their own in this sample.

A flagd feature-flag failure such as productCatalogFailure did not cause this: the flagd-config ConfigMap mounted read-only into the flagd Deployment lists productCatalogFailure (and every other fault flag) with defaultVariant "off", while the observed failures are explicit PostgreSQL 'password authentication failed for user "otelu"' errors from pq and psycopg2, not flag-driven status codes. Runtime flag toggles through the flagd UI are not observable with the available tools, so this rejection rests on the mounted flag file only.

Mechanism: the running PostgreSQL role otelu still holds the pre-rotation password (5-character value used by the revision-1 templates, which still authenticated successfully at 15:55:44.94Z), while the pod templates rolled out at 15:55:39-15:55:50Z present a 14-character password (the +9 character change seen in accounting and product-reviews, equal in length to 'otelp_7k9m2q4x' now stored in ConfigMap postgresql-init) and product-catalog was switched to a Secret-backed connection string; new connections therefore fail authentication and the internal catalog cache stays empty, so GetProduct returns 'Product Not Found' for every product.

The fault originates in ConfigMap astronomy-shop/postgresql-init: it is the only object in the namespace whose data defines the otelu database password, it was rewritten between 15:55:42Z and 15:55:47Z after PostgreSQL had already created the role from its earlier content at 15:54:58Z, and the client pod templates rolled out in the same seconds carry a password of exactly the length of the value it now holds, so the credential set published to the clients no longer matches the password the running database holds.

gaps: The actual password values cannot be read: the Secret referenced by product-catalog's DB_CONNECTION_STRING is not readable and both secretKeyRef name and key are redacted, and the literal passwords in accounting and product-reviews env are redacted, so the length comparison (5 vs 14 characters) is the only available evidence and the side holding the stale value cannot be proven.

The change itself was not observed: no change-history integration is available, so who or what rewrote ConfigMap postgresql-init and the three Deployment pod templates at 15:55:39-15:55:51Z, and the exact content written, is unknown; the two concurrent changes cannot be ordered with certainty from resourceVersion alone.

The successful product-reviews DB read at 15:55:44.94Z is a single sampled success; whether the pre-rollout credential would have continued to work after the 15:55:47Z credential change is unknown, and PostgreSQL does not log successful authentications to confirm or deny it.

The 'FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command' entry for backend pid 131 at 15:55:51.389Z has no visible cause; the statement that produced it is not logged, so a direct ALTER/pg_terminate_backend action on the database cannot be confirmed or excluded.

accounting was re-rolled to a 14-character DB credential at 15:55:47Z but no accounting error spans, DB writes or failed operations were observed; its impact is unknown, not established. A log query on that pod filtered to password|error|fail|Exception|pq returned no matching lines (query returned nothing), so its runtime logging state is also unknown.

Runtime flagd values are not observable: the flagd-config file shows every fault flag at defaultVariant "off", but flagd can be toggled at runtime through its UI and no tool here reads its runtime state.

Application telemetry only covers the last minutes: Jaeger is an in-memory backend and returned no traces for the 03:55Z or 09:55Z windows, and queries for frontend error traces in those hours returned nothing; the narrow metrics queries also returned nothing for product-catalog STATUS_CODE_ERROR and for a 13:56-15:56Z increase window, and the traces_span_metrics_calls_total series read 0 with only an end-of-window sample, so Prometheus span metrics could not be used to measure error rates or to determine when the deviation began.

product-reviews container log queries filtered to password|Exception|error|fail returned no matching lines (the query returned nothing) while its spans carry the psycopg2.OperationalError, so log-based corroboration for that pod is missing; product-catalog's product-catalog container had no log lines at all in the sampled window beyond the wait-for-postgresql line.

Services other than cart, checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy, product-catalog, product-reviews and recommendation were not checked (ad, currency, email, payment, shipping, quote, fraud-detection, image-provider, llm); their status in this incident is unknown.
next_steps: Read the Secret that supplies product-catalog's DB_CONNECTION_STRING and compare its password with ConfigMap postgresql-init and with the running database (e.g. test a connection as otelu) to establish which side is stale.

Reconcile the otelu credential: either ALTER USER otelu with the password the workloads are configured to use, or roll the workloads back to the credential the database still holds, then confirm that connections from product-catalog, product-reviews and accounting succeed.

Inspect the audit trail of the 15:55:39-15:55:51Z writes (ConfigMap postgresql-init and the accounting/product-reviews/product-catalog pod templates) to confirm the intended credential rotation and whether the database was supposed to be altered in the same step.
Verify accounting actually reaches PostgreSQL (its DB writes are exercised only by order placement, which currently fails earlier in checkout) before deciding whether it needs a fix as well.

service:
  extensions: [jaeger_storage, jaeger_query, healthcheckv2]
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [jaeger_storage_exporter]
  telemetry:
    resource:
      service.name: jaeger
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
        - periodic:
            interval: 10000
            timeout: 5000
            exporter:
              otlp:
                protocol: http/protobuf
                endpoint: http://${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_HOST}:${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_PORT_HTTP}
                insecure: true
    logs:
      level: info
extensions:
  healthcheckv2:
    use_v2: true
    http:
      endpoint: 0.0.0.0:13133
  jaeger_query:
    storage:
      traces: memory_backend
      metrics: metrics_backend
    base_path: /jaeger/ui
  jaeger_storage:
    backends:
      memory_backend:
        memory:
          max_traces: ${env:MEMORY_MAX_TRACES}
    metric_backends:
      metrics_backend:
        prometheus:
          endpoint: "http://${env:PROMETHEUS_ADDR}"
          normalize_calls: true
          normalize_duration: true

receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
